question.text: A particle leaves the origin with an initial velocity <math> <mrow> <mover accent="true"> <mtext>v</mtext> <mo>→</mo> </mover> <mo>=</mo> <mfenced close=")" open="(" separators=","> <mrow> <mtext>3.00</mtext> <mover accent="true"> <mtext>i</mtext> <mo>^</mo> </mover> </mrow> </mfenced> <msup> <mtext>ms</mtext> <mrow> <mo>-</mo> <mn>1</mn> </mrow> </msup> </mrow> </math> and a constant acceleration <math> <mrow> <mover accent="true"> <mtext>a</mtext> <mo>→</mo> </mover> <mo>=</mo> <mfenced close=")" open="(" separators=","> <mrow> <mo>-</mo> <mtext>1.00</mtext> <mover accent="true"> <mtext>i</mtext> <mo>^</mo> </mover> <mo>-</mo> <mtext>0.5</mtext> <mover accent="true"> <mtext>j</mtext> <mo>^</mo> </mover> </mrow> </mfenced> <msup> <mtext>ms</mtext> <mrow> <mo>-</mo> <mn>2</mn> </mrow> </msup> </mrow> </math> . When the particle reaches it maximum <math><mi>x</mi></math>-coordinate, what is the magnitude of its velocity (in m/s) in <math><mi>y</mi></math>-direction?

solution.text:
Velocity along x direction is

v x = v 0 2 + at

v x = 3 + - 1 t

so when particle reach maximum x coordinate v x = 0 ⇒ t = 3 sec

similarly   v y = v 0 y + a y t

                v y = 0 + - 1 2 t

               vyatt=3=-32=-1.5 m s-1
